evals.prompt: We need a board pack for the 14 October meeting on the depot automation options — the deck they'll see in the room, a paper to email beforehand, and the option model as a spreadsheet. Facts are in fixtures/board-pack/content.json. Build it and prove it rebuilds identically.
evals.expected_output: Runs build.py --prove on the fixture; delivers pptx, docx, xlsx, html review page and build-manifest.json; reports byte-identical hashes; every exhibit carries class and receipt; coverage-and-limits present.

evals.prompt: The COO revised the phased option: capex is now £28.5m and the annual saving £8.4m. Update the board pack but don't touch the design — the chair has already seen the look.
evals.expected_output: Runs revise.py with the two content changes; content version bumps; all outputs update including the exec-summary payback range; look_preserved true; no strikes; release clear.

evals.prompt: Change of plan: the pack won't be printed after all, it's screen-only on the boardroom display. Same content. What changes?
evals.expected_output: Runs revise.py with brief.setting.printed=false; reports manifest strike M3 with its flips; release blocked pending re-verdict; explains that the coach must re-confirm before the field/full-bleed decisions change.

evals.prompt: Make me a deck on the depot automation numbers. Nothing fancy, just make it look like a proper strategy deck.
evals.expected_output: Captures the brief (asks about setting/audience if absent), writes a verdict record with 2-3 candidate directions and a manifest, writes a deck spec with references only, builds with --prove, delivers with manifest. Does not type numbers into the spec.

evals.prompt: Same automation numbers, but this time it's the all-hands next Thursday — 2,000 people in the Leeds depot, most of them on the floor. Twelve minutes. They want to know if their jobs are safe. Make the deck.
evals.expected_output: Brief with purpose=inspire, setting live/not printed; verdict re-enters a deferred expressive direction or proposes one; deck spec uses keynote-cinematic with hero, big_number (headcount ceiling), closing; builds with --prove; the board's options are shown without a winner.
